name: PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk

frontmatter.title: DSSA: the parts, the covered siblings and the premium
frontmatter.summary: DSSA is a Sinar Mas conglomerate whose coal and telecom arms are separately listed. Restating the technology pillar for the merged, house-covered MORA and anchoring the balance sheet on June leaves the parts worth Rp188 in twelve months; the price is 3.6x that value. The konglo lens keeps part of the premium, giving Rp416 and a SELL. The parent has never paid a dividend.
thesis: The parts — the listed coal stake at the covered subsidiary's pre-lens fundamental value, the non-coal segments at audited net book, the unallocated remainder, net of non-controlling interests and less a holding-company discount — are worth Rp188 after twelve months, far below the Rp600 price.
The own-history P/E and P/BV are dropped, not down-weighted: they are struck on the price history OJK found manipulated and sit several times above the parts.

The upstream is real: the parent receives its controlling share of the October interim and is expected to receive the FY2026 final payable by June 2027, carried at face on the subsidiary's own modelled forward because a final is the established pattern. The parent has never paid a dividend to its own holders, so the discount is a hoarding discount and is charged at the wide end of the house band.

Power is marked at audited segment net assets because no external replacement-cost or regulated-asset estimate is published; the sensitivity to a lower book mark is disclosed, and technology is tested against its positive segment result.

The technology pillar is restated: the merged PT Ekamas Mora Republik is house-covered, so DSSA's 48.4% stake enters the parts at the covered subsidiary's pre-lens fundamental — the same rule applied to the coal stake — and the rest of the pillar stays at audited book net of the merged entity's assets.

PT Sinar Mas Tunggal, the controlling shareholder, is named by OJK as the DSSA-case recipient of the administrative fine over manipulation of trading in DSSA's own shares; the related parties have paid the penalties and the regulator says a criminal referral may follow. The konglo lens carries that finding as a flag that speeds the premium's closing and lowers the target, not one that slows it.

catalysts.event: DSSA begins a share buyback of {{fact.F95|idrtn}} that is scheduled to run until 18 January 2027
OJK hands the sanction letters over in person to the sanctioned parties, including the controlling shareholder, and to nine exchange members
The regulator describes its market-conduct sanctions as the largest in its history and keeps criminal escalation open
OJK confirms the administrative fines in the DSSA, BREN and CUAN cases have been paid in full to the state treasury by the related parties, not the issuers
OJK publishes its year-to-date enforcement list naming PT Sinar Mas Tunggal in the DSSA case
The OJK chair says the parties facing criminal sanctions may be announced within the week

At the BEI Media Gathering in Mandalika, OJK says it is calculating restitution for investors affected by the DSSA, BREN and CUAN share cases, with no amount, no timing and no payer stated and the mechanism still unconfirmed; reported on 5 November 2026
The exchange removes the HSC names, including DSSA and its coal subsidiary GEMS, from the IHSG calculation and redistributes their index weight to the remaining constituents

OJK says it has completed its study of investor-loss recovery through disgorgement, anchored in Article 100E of the 2026 financial-sector law amendment, with no amount, eligible-investor list or payment schedule announced for the three cases
OJK's 2026 enforcement list is published in full detail, recording the sanctions in the DSSA case against PT Sinar Mas Tunggal and the fines on each of the eight broker-dealers, plus the case period

DSSA's third-quarter 2026 financial statements are due, and the company has said they will be audited — the first audited interim in the record and the dated test of the June minority and technology balances
IDX minimum free-float step takes effect for large caps; DSSA's free float clears the raised minimum but the group remains in the HSC regime

GEMS free float of {{fact.F102|pctv}} must reach the first step of {{fact.F106|pctv}}; a new-share remedy of about {{fact.F103|usdm}} is carried at a fifty per cent probability in the subsidiary's model
MSCI consultation on moving Indonesia to Standalone status closes, with a decision due by 30 June 2027
MSCI decides whether to adopt the Standalone proposal; rejection would lift the index-increase freeze and re-open the HSC names to passive flows
GEMS FY2026 final dividend is payable by the IDX norm, the second upstream receipt inside the valuation window

blocks.text: **The view.** The parts, not the OJK-tainted multiples, set the value: the coal and telecom stakes at the covered subsidiaries' pre-lens fundamentals, the non-coal segments at audited net book, plus the unallocated remainder, net of minorities and less a holdco discount, give Rp188 a share in twelve months, or Rp166 today [S0, S20]. The price is Rp600; the konglo lens keeps part of that premium because a float of 21.5% sets the marginal price, and across the regime scenarios the target is Rp416, a -30.7% return, rating SELL [S0].

**What this revision changes.** The merged PT Ekamas Mora Republik is house-covered, so DSSA's 48.4% stake enters at the covered subsidiary's pre-lens fundamental — Rp221 a share on 47,774m shares — and the rest of the pillar stays at audited book net of the merged entity's 1,146 USD m, cutting the pillar by about a quarter and the parts by about a tenth [S35, S36, S9]. The FY2026E balance sheet is anchored on June actuals for debt, cash, net debt and capex; the minority line remains a forecast roll, labelled in section three [S0, S6].

**The enforcement record.** The related parties, not the issuers, paid the OJK fines in full — IDR2.10tn across the three cases, IDR1.50tn DSSA-related — and restitution is statutory under Article 100E but no amount, payer or schedule is announced [S21, S33, F121-F123]. No release names DSSA as payer, so no line moves; the finding sits once, in the lens [S10, S14].

**The variant view.** The market pays a 3.6x premium to the whole, not for the coal arm in its separately listed subsidiary or the non-coal parts at book [S0, S20]. The lens explains why the premium persists — thin float, index deletions and a live sanction — but does not make it value [S15, S16, S10]. The nearest bull catalyst is a first distribution from DSSA to its own holders, not a first upstream, which already happens [S9].

DSSA reports in dollars and describes itself as an energy and infrastructure company [S9]. Revenue comes from four segments — captive steam and electricity, fertilizer and chemicals trading, coal mining and trading, and cable television, internet and technology — plus small renewable and other lines [S9]. Coal dominates: mining and trading revenue was 2,488 USD m of group 2,791.2, almost nine-tenths, through PT Golden Energy Mines Tbk, listed since 2011, in which DSSA holds 51.0%; the mines operate under coal contracts of work, whose royalty and permit terms the group flags as a margin risk [S9, S0, S3].

Technology revenue was 212 USD m last year and 170 USD m in the first half, roughly double, and fertilizer and chemicals 90.9 USD m; power has no external revenue because the fee is earned inside the group [S9, S6]. The 2026 MoraRepublic merger moved the telecom assets into PT Ekamas Mora Republik, listed and house-covered, in which DSSA holds 48.4% through PT Innovate Mas Utama; the merged entity's 1,146 USD m of assets sit inside the segment's 2,208 USD m [S35, S36, S9]. The group says the energy pillar funds the build-out of the others, its stated reason for not paying a dividend [S6, S9].

PT Sinar Mas Tunggal holds 59.9%; public and treasury shares together are 40.1%, of which treasury 19.7%, leaving a public float in the low twenties [S9]. The lens uses the datapack's 21.5% registry figure [S0].

DSSA is five businesses, and the house card says mark each on its own terms rather than apply a blanket multiple [S9]. The largest is thermal coal, and the coal price reaches DSSA through the listed subsidiary's own quote and fundamental rather than a mine model built here [S9, S12]. Power is a captive processing fee with a large asset base and no external revenue, chemicals a low-margin distribution book, and digital infrastructure — broadband, homepasses and a data-centre build — the fastest-growing line [S6, S9].

The group is a follower: the coal producer is mid-curve, broadband and data centres face far larger incumbents, and chemicals is a price-taker [S9, S6]. Two external influences matter: the market-conduct file, read as manipulation-class [S10, S14], and the coal royalty and permit regime, which reaches our target through the subsidiary's model [S9].

Revenue fell to 2,791.2 from 3,017.8 and gross margin to 33.7% from 40.7%; parent net profit was 230.5, of which minorities took 130.7, and return on equity was 16.0% [S0, S9]. The data pack's depreciation is a fraction of the real charge because the direct-method cash flow carries no add-back; the segment note discloses consolidated D&A of 78.2 USD m and 83.6 USD m, and the model carries that restated charge [S9].

The forecast is built from the reported first half and the subsidiary's covered plan [S0, S9, S20]. The first half ran US$1,770.0m of revenue, up roughly a third, with coal up nearly thirty per cent and technology up nearly ninety [S6]. The subsidiary prices FY2026 at the house coal deck's FY2026E marker, close to a quarter above FY2025A, on its 58Mt plan against the 55.0Mt realised in 2025 [S20, S12]. Revenue grows 30.0% to 3,628.6; gross margin of 40.7% is the subsidiary's own modelled margin, and the group-wide ratio does not overstate the non-coal parts, whose audited segment result on their own revenue is above the coal column's margin [S9, F112-F115]. EBITDA is 875.1 at a 24.1% margin and parent profit 373.1, with the second half at the subsidiary's run-rate rather than a collapse [S6, S20, S0]. FY2027E growth of -14.0% follows the lower FY2027E marker on flat volume, and the top line is held after because no source supports a further decline [S20].
Capex of 1,005.2 against EBITDA of 875.1 leaves free cash flow to the firm of -184.0, against a negative -99.4 last year: spending absorbs essentially all the businesses generate [S0, S9].

**The balance sheet, anchored on June.** At 30 June 2026 gross debt was 1,911.1, cash 814.4 — the narrower release line is 723 USD m, the difference being short-term placements — and net debt 1,096.7, against 910.6 a year earlier [S0, S6]. Net borrowing and capex are set so the year-end lines equal the June actuals, and interest follows the opening debt at the FY2025 effective rate [S0, S6]. Segment liabilities of 2,121 USD m are within two per cent of consolidated liabilities, assets of 4,415 USD m less equity of 2,261 USD m [S9].

**The minority line is a forecast roll, not the June actual.** The engine's line runs from 444.4 at FY2025A to 655.9 in FY2026E. The pack's 30 June balance sheet carries a minority roughly double the audited year-end 444 USD m, most of the increase the MORA consolidation of an entity with 1,146 USD m of assets; total equity of 3,050 USD m is the parent and minority sum [S0, S35, S6]. The roll is not calibrated to June because the engine derives it from the year's minority profit share and dividends and carries no acquisition-date minority line; it is not used in the valuation, whose deduction is the audited FY2025 split [S9, F77, F78]. Debt, cash and net debt are calibrated because they are the opening balances the funding waterfall runs from [S0, S6].

**Earnings quality.** Accruals are negative in two of the last three years: operating cash was 330 USD m, 693 USD m and 1,031 USD m against net profit of 361.2, 542.8 and 865.3 [S0, S9]. Free cash flow to the firm is negative in all three (-99.4, -139.4, 307.6), a capital-spending story, and technology assets grew from 1,162 USD m to 2,208 USD m in a year [S0, S9]. Related-party purchases were 0.4% of cost of revenues and 0.9% of G&A, mainly family property, telecom and insurance; the data-centre build runs through PT LG Sinarmas at Rp1.2tn [S9, F67]. No PSAK 16 revaluation surplus remains; these and the two splits, the stake restructuring, the elimination column of -1,954 USD m and the treasury block of 1,516 million shares are optics-class, while the manipulation finding is manipulation-class and sits at the controller [S9, S10, S13, S14].

The house card values a holding company on its parts, less holdco net debt and a discount the base rate says persists [S0]. The parts carry 100% of the blend; the own-history P/E and P/BV are dropped because both sat several times above the parts and are struck on the tape OJK found manipulated [S0, S10, S13, S14]. Cost of equity is 12.6% and WACC 10.7% [S0].

**The parts.** The coal stake is at the covered subsidiary's pre-lens fundamental Rp6,094/share, not its quote Rp7,150/share or its post-lens target Rp6,661/share: a covered subsidiary enters the parent at its fundamental, or its regime premium would be counted twice [S20, VAL_KONGLO_REGIME §4]. DSSA holds 51.0% [S20]. The merged MORA stake follows the same rule at Rp221 [S36]. Steam and electricity, other technology, fertilizer, chemicals and renewable energy are at audited net book; the elimination column and non-controlling interests are deductions [S9, S36].

**Power and technology.** Power has no external revenue and no reliable segment result — the FY2024 comparative was -0.2m — so no earnings multiple can be struck; it is marked at audited net assets 2,659 USD m less 668 USD m, with the affiliate sale of the plants showing revaluation movements of 111m and 160 USD m through equity and no impairment on what remains [S9]. Technology is the merged entity at Rp221 on 47,774m shares, plus the remaining pay-TV and data-centre assets at audited book: no segmental operating profit is published, so book at par is the most likely mark [S36, S9].

**The reconciliation.** Consolidated equity 2,261 USD m includes non-controlling interests of 444 USD m, of which the coal subsidiary is 350 USD m; the non-GEMS minority is deducted directly and the GEMS book slice in the other parts is removed with it, so the book is not double-counted [S9, F77, F78]. The parts carry the 48.4% MORA stake, not the June segment book, so the June minority does not enter a year-end book valuation [S9, S35, S36].

**The discount.** The base rate is a holdco discount of twenty to forty per cent persisting indefinitely; a narrower discount needs a dated catalyst that upstreams cash — the card's dividend-upstream law, not a peer comparison [S0, S9]. The policy permits up to 30.0% of net profit and the parent has never paid a dividend to its own holders, saying its subsidiaries need the capital: the card's definition of a holdco deserving the widest discount in its range [S9]. Two buybacks are the only evidence against it, and neither is recurring, so we charge 40%, the wide end [S9, F44-F47, S28].

**The upstream.** GEMS paid a US$200.0m FY2026 interim on 22 October 2026, after the balance-sheet date, of which DSSA's 51.0% is US$102.0m, carried in the bridge [S25, F88, F96]. The subsidiary also prices a FY2026 final at Rp805/share, DSSA's share being the second receipt; it is not declared, so it is carried at face, probability one, because GEMS paid a final for FY2023 and FY2024 and the October interim, leaving timing rather than occurrence as the risk [F60, F61, F88] [S20]. Neither is inside the GEMS mark [S9, S0].

The sum of the parts is Rp166 a share; grown at the cost of equity for a year it is Rp188, probability-weighted across the business scenarios Rp188, the fundamental the lens uses [S0]. The price Rp600 is 3.6x today's value [S0].

**The konglo lens.** The engine measures a log premium of 1.3 and assumes only part closes because the marginal price is set by float: 21.5% of the capital trades [S0, S9]. The HSC listing, index exits and live sanction push the closing share up, not down: they keep the float thin and the marginal buyer local, so more of the gap closes and the target is lower [S15, S16, S10, S14]. The deck charges 5% for HSC status and 10% for the enforcement finding on the closing share [S0]. Three regime scenarios base-weighted at 50%: bear closes 85% for Rp227, base 45% for Rp380, bull closes none and holds Rp676; weighted, the target is Rp416 [S0].

**What the price implies.** The reverse DCF cannot solve the price inside the discount range: the price sits above the undiscounted parts, so no positive discount brackets it — the market pays a premium, not a discount [S0, S20].

**Look-through earnings and leverage.** DSSA's look-through earnings are US$131.7m, the 51.0% share of the coal subsidiary's FY2025A parent profit, against reported parent profit of US$230.5 [S20, S0, S9]. The FY2025A consolidated balance sheet carried net debt of 910.6, 1.9x FY2025A EBITDA, at the parent and the non-coal parts, so it is already deducted in the net-book marks [S20, S0, S9, F43].
The grid reports pre-lens values and brackets neither the target nor the price [S0].

The engine can only shock the holdco discount, because a covered holding cannot be re-priced inside a DSSA scenario, so the table's cases are discount scenarios [S0]. **Bear** (25%): the governance file escalates, the coal marker normalises and the discount widens by the same margin beyond the wide end of the band, giving Rp139 today and Rp156 in twelve months [S0]. The conditional asset tail is stated, not modelled: at the subsidiary's own bear target of Rp2,018/share the controlling stake is worth about a third of its base mark, and a ten per cent haircut to the two fallback book marks takes the fundamental down roughly two-fifths before the lens [S20, S9]. That tail, not the discount shock, is why the bear weight is 25%; capitalised, the weighted fundamental would be about a tenth below Rp188 and the target below Rp416 [S0, S20]. The business and regime sets are combined under the konglo card's independence convention, disclosed because a governance escalation or a coal-price fall plausibly drives both; positive correlation makes the joint bear likelier, not rarer, and the joint bull is treated the same way [S0, S20]. **Bull**: a dated capital-allocation signal — the GEMS FY2026 final payable by 30 June 2027, the buyback completing, a first dividend to DSSA holders or a stake sale — narrows the discount, with the 58Mt plan delivered and technology doubling, giving Rp194 and Rp219 against a base at 50% [S6, S9, S12, S20, S28]. The bull narrows the discount by the same margin the bear widens it, so the two are the same size in opposite directions with equal weights [S0].

**The subsidiary's bull face and free-float step.** GEMS's own bull target is Rp12,109/share and its quote Rp7,150/share, against the pre-lens mark Rp6,094/share and the post-lens target Rp6,661/share [S20]. At the bull target the GEMS row roughly doubles, taking the fundamental to about half again today's Rp188 while the lens target stays below the Rp600 [S20, S36]. GEMS's free float is 10.1% against the 12.5% first step due 31 March 2027, inside DSSA's window; the subsidiary carries a new-share remedy of about US$55.1m at a fifty per cent probability, of which DSSA's share is about US$28.1m, roughly one per cent of the parts, and that dilution sits inside the GEMS mark [S20, F102, F106, S19].

**Tails outside every mark.** The cross-guarantee stack is facility plafon, not drawn balances, so a call on it is a bear tail sized on the maximum [S9, F63-F66]. The criminal and restitution tail is unquantified: OJK may announce criminal parties and has completed its study of investor-loss recovery, while stating no amount, timing or payer [S27, S31, S33]. If levied on the controller it is a funding call on the shareholder; if charged to the issuer it is an unquantified liability; if to the brokers it is outside the group [S9, F74].

**Five risks carry weight.** Governance (high/high): the controlling shareholder has been fined over manipulation of DSSA's shares, the related parties have paid, and the criminal track remains open [S14, S10, S13, S21, S26, S27]. Capital allocation (high/high): capex absorbs essentially all of group EBITDA, the parent receives distributions but has never paid a dividend, and the D-Hub land purchase is the same pattern in one transaction [S0, S9, S28, S29]. Coal-market (medium/medium): a lower marker lowers the largest part directly [S9, S20]. Disclosure (high/medium): no segmental operating profit is published for the largest book-value segments [S9]. Currency (medium/medium): the group reports in dollars, so the rupiah value of the parts moves with the exchange rate while the businesses do not [S0].
A dated action that distributes cash to DSSA's own shareholders would justify a narrower discount [S9], while a criminal escalation widens it [S13, S10].

**The konglo profile.** DSSA is the Sinar Mas group's energy and infrastructure holding, the Widjaja family's listed vehicle and parent of the separately listed coal miner; the controlling holding company holds 59.9% and treasury is 19.7% [S9]. The lens uses the datapack's 21.5% registry figure [S0]. DSSA's float is compliant, but GEMS is 10.1% free against the 12.5% first step due 31 March 2027 [S20, F102, F106]. DSSA and GEMS were removed from the IHSG calculation on 2 November 2026 and from the MSCI and FTSE indexes in 2026; the exchange and OJK press HSC issuers to refloat [S15, S16, S17, S30].

**The enforcement file.** The OJK manipulation sanction against PT Sinar Mas Tunggal, the 59.9% controlling shareholder, is the largest in the regulator's history [S13, S14]. The sanction letter is dated 16 October 2026 and covers conduct from 12 January 2024 to 3 February 2026; OJK sanctioned 9 exchange members, warned eight sales staff, froze one underwriter representative's licence and named the shareholder on the 1 November enforcement list [S32, S34, S26, F116-F120]. On 30 October OJK confirmed the related parties, not the issuers, had paid the fines in full: IDR2.10tn across the three cases, the DSSA share IDR1.50tn [S21]. The regulator will escalate to a criminal investigation if the evidence supports one, calls the conduct a criminal market-manipulation act, and continues to summon individual and foreign corporate parties; the OJK chair says the parties facing criminal sanctions may be announced within the week under the una via principle [S13, S21, S27, F82]. On 5 November OJK said its study of investor-loss recovery through disgorgement is complete, resting on Article 100E of the 2026 financial-sector law amendment, with no amount, eligible-investor list or schedule announced [S31, S33, F121-F123]. It names no payer, and the fines paid came from the related parties, so no liability is attributed to DSSA; a mechanism reaching the issuer's balance sheet is the governance question the development opens, not a base-case cost [S21, S31, S33]. On the house framework this is a manipulation-class flag, routed by the konglo card to the regime lens and counted once there [S10, S14].

**Structure flags.** Cross-guarantees are disclosed contingent claims, not netted in the parts [S9, F63-F66]. Treasury: the 2023 buyback left 1,516 million shares, 19.7% of issued capital, and the live IDR1.00tn buyback will add to it; at Rp600 it retires shares above fundamental value, a small transfer from continuing holders to sellers [S9, S28, S0]. Pledges: GEMS-group shares and receivables secure the subsidiary's bank facilities, and no pledge of the controlling shareholder's DSSA stake is disclosed [S9, F74]. Related-party assets: the data-centre build runs through PT LG Sinarmas Technology Solutions at Rp1.2tn [S9, F67], and on 29 October 2026 BSDE unit Surya Inter Wisesa contracted to sell 16.6 ha in the D-Hub SEZ at BSD City to DSSA unit SMPlus Cakrawala Cipta Gemilang for Rp3.1tn, 5.7% of the group's 30 June equity and just under the independent appraisal of Rp3.12tn, an affiliate transaction the appraiser found fair [S23, S29, F89]. It is contracted after the balance-sheet date, so it is outside the audited segment books; it converts cash to land at the appraisal and adds no project value because no return is disclosed [S29].

**Dividend and ESG.** The policy permits up to 30.0% of net profit and the parent has paid none to its own shareholders, on the stated explanation that its subsidiaries require the capital [S9]. The subsidiary does pay, and the parent receives the controlling share [S9, F58-F61]. An upstream that arrives at the parent and stops there is the whole cost of the structure — a hoarding discount — and it is why the dividend-yield method is dropped and the discount is charged at the wide end of the band [S0, S9]. On ESG the exposures are the ordinary ones for Indonesian thermal coal at the subsidiary plus the governance sanction, on which this name would not pass a controlling-shareholder conduct screen today [S10, S9, S6].

The enforcement chronology is in section six [S14, S21, S26, S32, S33]. The HSC names left the IHSG calculation on 2 November 2026 — 81 of them, DSSA and GEMS included — and OJK says the status alone carries no sanction while active names face review [S16, S30]. The buyback runs to 18 January 2027 [S28]; the IDX free-float step and GEMS's lift from 10.1% to 12.5% both land on 31 March 2027 [S19, S20, F106]; the MSCI Standalone consultation closes on 30 April 2027 with a decision by 30 June 2027 [S22].

**The one scheduled filing that tests the numbers.** The company has said its third-quarter 2026 financial statements will be audited — unusual for an IDX interim, where the quarterly LK is reviewed rather than audited, and the source gives no reason [S6]. It is the first dated test of the two balances this revision reconstructed: the June minority position, which the model carries only as an FY2026E forecast roll, and the technology pillar's book. A qualified opinion or a restated June minority would move the deduction in section four; a clean opinion would confirm the MORA bridge in section three [S6, S9, S35].
What we watch: a first parent dividend or stake sale, segmental operating profit for technology and power, and any restitution amount naming DSSA as payer [S9, S31].

bear.narrative: Mirrored on the only driver the engine can shock for a parts valuation: the holdco discount moves ten points, to 50% here and to 30% in the bull, from a base of 40% [S0, S9]. The base sits at the wide end of the house band because the parent has never paid a dividend, so a mirrored ten-point bear necessarily lands beyond it: the fifty per cent is a disclosed stress beyond the band, not a claim about peer practice [S0, S9]. The engine marks a covered holding at its pre-lens fundamental and cannot re-price it inside a scenario, so the asset tails are stated with the same sourced marks and are not forced into the discount shock: at the subsidiary's own bear target the 51% stake is worth about a third of its base mark (USD334m against USD1,010m), and a ten per cent haircut to the two fallback book marks (power and the residual technology assets) is the same ten-per-cent direction [S20, S9]. The MSCI proposal is adopted at the 30 June 2027 decision, moving Indonesia to Standalone and removing the index-increase freeze's upside rather than lifting it [S22]. The governance file escalates to a criminal investigation and the Rp6.42tn cross-guarantee plafon becomes a live claim inside the same tail [S9, F63-F66]. The bear weight is 25%, matched to the bull: the probability of the bear is not raised above the bull to carry the asset tail, because the tail is disclosed at full strength rather than capitalised in the table. The business and regime sets are combined under the konglo card's independence convention, not because the two are believed independent for this name: a governance escalation or a coal-price fall plausibly drives both, and §5 shows the positively-correlated joint-bear sensitivity.

bull.narrative: Built from the bull drivers, and the coal sibling's own bull is the largest of them. The subsidiary's published bull target is Rp12,181 a share against a pre-lens fundamental of Rp6,094, so at that mark the 51% stake would be worth about USD2,019m against the USD1,010m carried — the same two-sided sensitivity the bear leg discloses on the subsidiary's bear target [S20]. The engine cannot re-price the covered holding inside a DSSA scenario, so the mark is disclosed rather than forced into the discount; the table's bull is the discount, the upstream and the index-relief branch. The coal subsidiary delivers its 58Mt plan [S12, S20]; the FY2026 final dividend is paid by 30 June 2027 and the buyback running to 18 January 2027 is repeated, or a first dividend at DSSA itself finally upstreams cash to the parent's holders [S9, F44, S28]. The MSCI Standalone proposal is rejected at the 30 June 2027 decision and the index-increase freeze is lifted, re-opening the HSC names to passive flows [S22]. The discount narrows ten points to 30%, back inside the card's 20-40% band and the mirror of the bear [S0, S9]. The data-centre/technology option is deliberately not credited above book: the D-Hub parcel is carried at the independent appraisal (the purchase price sits just below it), the flagship AI-ready data-centre project has no disclosed return, and no segment-return disclosure exists, so any uplift would be invented [S29, F92-F94, S9]. Even here the parts do not reach the market's price.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs holding-company discount and cost of equity

adjustments.why: on the exchange's HSC list (as of 2026-10-22): out of the IHSG, the LQ45/IDX30/IDX80 and the MSCI indexes [konglo deck S3]
OJK found trading manipulation (2026-10-16) [konglo deck S7]

groups.name: Sinar Mas group (Widjaja family)
groups.role: energy and infrastructure holding company; parent of GEMS

index_deletions.note: deleted at the May 2026 review; AMRT moved to Small Cap

enforcement.note: planned, structured trading manipulation of DSSA shares in 2023-2026 that pushed the price up; PT SMT fined Rp1.5tn, brokers fined and sales staff warned

konglo.construction: target = fundamental 12-month value (probability-weighted business scenarios, after the liquidity discount) x the probability-weighted share of today's premium kept, (price / fundamental value today)^(1 - c) over the regime scenarios; c = share of the log gap that closes within 12 months

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is anchored on the reported first half and the subsidiary's own plan, not on a fade. The first half, reported through S6 (which describes the interim as audited; the LK itself is not archived), ran revenue at USD 1.77bn, up 34.0%, with coal up 29.8% and technology up 89.3% [S6]; the listed coal subsidiary's own covered model carries FY2026E revenue up 33% on the 58Mt plan and the house coal deck's FY2026E marker (137.0 against 108.4 in FY2025) [S20, S12, F48]. Coal is roughly nine-tenths of group revenue [S9, F7], so a 30% consolidated step is the subsidiary-consistent path and is the revenue-growth clamp for this template. FY2027E falls 14% for a sourced reason, not a hand-set fade: the same subsidiary model and deck carry the FY2027E coal marker 14% below FY2026E on a flat 58Mt volume [S20]. From FY2028E the top line is held at the FY2027E level because no source supports a further decline; the path feeds only the small earnings cross-checks and does not set the target, which is the sum of the parts.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Follows the covered coal subsidiary's own modelled gross margin, because the subsidiary is roughly nine-tenths of group revenue and holding last year's ratio against a 26% higher FY2026E coal marker would be the unsourced squeeze the most-likely rule forbids [S9, S20]. The subsidiary's model carries FY2026E gross margin of 40.7% (FY2025A 31.9%), fading to 34.5% in FY2027E and 31.2% in FY2028E on the house coal deck's marker path (137.0 then 118.0) [S20]. DSSA's own FY2025A consolidated gross margin was 33.7% against the subsidiary's 31.9%, so the group carries a small non-coal premium; we use the subsidiary's ratios directly rather than add one, which leaves the forecast slightly below the group's own FY2025A relationship. From FY2028E the ratio is held at the last modelled year — no source supports a further move.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: The last audited year's own ratio of SG&A and other operating expense to revenue [S0], held flat in real terms. The group's overhead carries the technology, chemicals and corporate functions as well as the mine, and nothing in the LK sources a step down; a decline would be an unsourced haircut.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Set from the LK's OWN depreciation and amortisation, not the data pack's cash-flow feed: the group reports consolidated D&A of USD 78.2m for FY2025 and USD 83.6m for FY2024 in the segment note [F17, F18], roughly three times the pack's direct-method figure, and the ratio of that restated charge to revenue is what the forecast carries. The pack's D&A is small because the IDX cash-flow statement is prepared on the direct method and carries no add-back.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is set from the reported half-year balance sheet, not from a plan: cash rose USD238.85m while gross debt rose USD424.95m and profit was positive, which is only consistent with investment above the FY2025 rate, and the ratio that reproduces the 30 June 2026 actual debt and cash is 27.7% of revenue [S0, S6]. From FY2027E the ratio returns to the last audited year's 16.7% [S0, S9] because no source supports the build peak persisting; the group spends across the mine, the power assets, the broadband network and the data-centre build.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: The 30 June 2026 balance sheet already shows the release: operating working capital stood at USD 477.8m against USD 610.8m at the FY2025A year-end [S0, latest_bs 2026-06-30], after the audited first half [S6]. Holding that dollar level — not the three-year average ratio, which the FY2023 commodity peak distorts — makes FY2026E NWC fall to USD 477.8m and then stay flat, so the FCFF release is the one already visible on the reported balance sheet rather than a second, unsourced assumption. Every later year's ratio is set to reproduce the same USD 477.8m at that year's revenue.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(tax, pbt))

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: Set at the FY2025A effective rate of 5.87% (interest expense USD 71.37m on opening debt USD 1,216.33m) rather than the three-year average of 6.66%, which carries the FY2023 rate when debt was much smaller. The last actual is the sourced rate on the current debt stack [S0, S9].

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_income, cash[-1]))

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: FY2026E carries the H1-2026 actual increase, not a fabricated financing plan: gross debt rose from USD1,486.164m at 31 December 2025 to USD1,911.111m at 30 June 2026, so the year is anchored on +USD424.946m and held flat thereafter [S0, S6]. The reported half-year shows the group funded a cash build and a heavy investment programme with new debt, which is why the forecast no longer assumes deleveraging. The engine charges interest on the opening balance, so the full-year cost of the new debt appears from FY2027E.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Held at the FY2025A actual of USD 44.157m rather than the engine's zero default: the last audited year earned a positive other non-operating line and nothing in the FY2025 accounts or the H1-2026 release sources a step to zero. Carrying the last actual is the most-likely rule; zeroing it was an unsourced haircut that depressed FY2026E parent profit below the reported first half [S0, S9].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Set at the FY2025A actual ratio of 36.18% (minority interest USD 130.662m on net profit USD 361.20m) rather than the three-year average of 43.33%, which is inflated by FY2023 when the coal subsidiary earned a peak-year profit. The most-likely rule is to reproduce the last audited year's split; the three-year average quietly raised the minority cut by seven points and pushed FY2026E parent profit below the reported H1-2026 actual [S0, S9].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Zero, and sourced rather than assumed by omission: the group's policy permits a distribution of up to 30% of net profit [F14], but the accounts record no dividend payment in any reported year [S0, S9] and the company states it has not distributed dividends because its subsidiaries require substantial capital expenditure [S9]. A payout we cannot source, on a name that has never paid one, would be a fabricated leg in the blend; the engine therefore drops the yield method entirely.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: The primary method is a sum of the parts with a holding-company discount, so no perpetual growth rate reaches the target; this input only frames the cross-checks. It is set at the house's long-run USD inflation assumption, below the house cap for a USD-reporting name, because a coal-heavy conglomerate should not be assigned perpetual real growth.

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: Charged at the wide end of the house holdco band, on the card's dividend-upstream law rather than on a hope of narrowing. The base rate for holdco and SOTP names is that a discount of 20-40% persists indefinitely, and a narrower discount needs a NAMED, DATED catalyst that actually upstreams cash. The parent has never paid a dividend to its own holders and states that it keeps the capital in its subsidiaries because they need the spending [S9]; that is the card's definition of a holdco that deserves the widest discount in its range. The two capital-return precedents — the 2023 buyback of 154,105,327 shares for USD 483.8m, part reissued in 2024 [S9, F44, F45], and the Rp1tn buyback running from 19 October 2026 to 18 January 2027 [S28] — are small against market value (the live one is about a hundredth of it) and neither is a recurring distribution, so neither passes the dated-upstream test. We charge 40%, the wide end of the card's 20-40% base rate, because the hoarding law sets this name's warranted discount: the parent receives the subsidiary's dividends and passes none on, which the card says deserves the widest discount in its range. No peer distribution is used; the band is the house base rate, not a comp set. The governance file — related-party purchases of family property, telecom and insurance, the data-centre package bought from a family affiliate, the treasury overhang and the cross-guarantees [S9, F46-F67] — widens it further and is NOT the OJK trading sanction; the OJK manipulation finding is assigned once, to the konglo lens (enforcement_manipulation), per the konglo card, and is not counted again here. The 2023 and 2026 buybacks are the only evidence against the widest end, and they do not carry a distribution.

challenges.challenge: The technology segment (1,094 net book, 44% of gross parts) is marked at audited FY2025 net book, but since the 22 April 2026 merger DSSA's technology pillar holds the listed Ekamas Mora Republik (MORA.JK), which this house covers: S6 lists the MORA and Eka Mas Republik merger into PT Ekamas Mora Republik Tbk among DSSA's own Q2-2026 corporate actions, and MORA.JK's covered model carries tp_fundamental 221.49 against a 1,595 price (7.2x). VAL_KONGLO_REGIME section 4 requires a covered listed subsidiary to enter the parent at its pre-lens house fundamental; that rule is applied to GEMS and not here, and the report never names MORA, DSSA's post-merger stake, or MORA's coverage.
challenges.answer: Technology pillar restated. The merged PT Ekamas Mora Republik is house-covered, so the konglo covered-subsidiary rule applies to it exactly as to the coal stake: DSSA's 48.36% is marked at MORA's pre-lens fundamental of Rp221.487823 a share on 47,774.192736m shares (USD282.67m), and the residual pillar stays at audited book net of EMR's USD1,146.17m assets (USD526.28m). The pillar falls 26% and the gross parts 12%; the target falls to the mid-400s, a sixteenth below the published figure [S35, S36, S9, F124-F126, F129].

challenges.challenge: The business bull gives the coal sibling's own bull zero credit. GEMS's covered model carries a bull target of 12,181 against a base of 6,591 (S20), i.e. 1.85x, while the DSSA bear leg explicitly quotes GEMS's bear (2,018, 0.33x) and says it would take the marked parts down a third. The DSSA bull (243, +17%) is therefore a discount-only bull and excludes the driver behind 41% of gross parts, so the method card's mirrored-shock rule is broken in one direction only.
challenges.answer: Both covered sibling marks are now two-sided in section five: the GEMS row at its bull target of 12,109.4 (about double the pre-lens mark, fundamental to roughly half again) and at its bear target of 2,017.6 (about a third, parts down nearly a third), with the same rule disclosed for MORA and the engine's inability to re-price a holding inside a scenario stated rather than hidden [S20, S36].

challenges.challenge: Power is 45% of gross parts (1,991) and is marked at 1.0x audited segment net assets, the top of the report's own disclosed 0.5-1.0x range, for a segment with no external revenue and no FY2025 segment result (the FY2025 segment-result row sums to 941.7 with no power column; FY2024 was -0.17). VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT forbids a blanket book mark for an unlisted segment, and the published sensitivity grid (discount +/-10pp, COE +/-1pp) does not include this mark at all: at 0.5x book the fundamental falls to about Rp115, -38%.
challenges.answer: Power stays at 1.0x audited segment net assets. The only transaction evidence the record carries is the sale of the plants to PT Indah Kiat and PT Pindo Deli, an affiliate disposal with the revaluation movements taken through equity and no impairment disclosed on the remainder; nothing in it supports a mark below book, and no regulated-asset-base or replacement cost is published. The 0.5-1.0x range and its size (half book roughly halves the fundamental) are now stated in the prose, because the sensitivity grid is fixed by the industry config, which this desk cannot edit [S9, F23, F24, F49, F76].

challenges.challenge: The lens flags' sign is stated backwards. Section 4 says 'The closing share is slowed by HSC listing, exit from the IHSG and the index family, and the live sanction', and the thesis repeats that 'the konglo lens slows the premium's compression rather than removing it'. The engine adds the adjustments to the closing share for a premium (comp = compress + adj; deck 0.30 base + 0.05 hsc + 0.10 enforcement = 0.45), so the flags SPEED the closing and LOWER the target: without the 0.15 the probability-weighted target would be about Rp494, not Rp429.
challenges.answer: Lens direction corrected in section four and in the thesis: HSC status, the IHSG and index exits and the sanction raise the closing share, and the deck's 10% HSC plus 10% enforcement adjustments together take roughly an eighth off the lens target. The previous prose described the numbers' opposite [S0, S15, S16, S30].

challenges.challenge: Leverage is carried at the FY2025 balance sheet against a half-year actual that has moved a long way: gross debt 1,911.1 at 30 Jun 2026 against the model's FY2026E 1,486.2 (held flat) and net debt 1,096.7 against section 4's '910.6, 1.9x EBITDA'. The model's FY2026E net debt of 698.6 therefore assumes about 398 of H2 deleveraging that no source supports. With capex at 16.7% of revenue, negative FCFF in recent years, a funding waterfall whose fourth rung is new shares and 19.7% already in treasury, the per-share risk is a placement - and the section never sizes it.
challenges.answer: FY2026E recalibrated to the 30 June 2026 actual: debt 1,911.1, cash 814.4 (narrow line 723.3), net debt 1,096.7, capex 1,005.2, FCFF -184.0, interest 87.2 rising to 112.1 in FY2027E. The unsourced 398 of H2 deleveraging is gone, and section five sizes the new-shares rung at the FY2026E net borrowing of 424.9 [S0, S6].

challenges.challenge: The Q3-2026 audited interim is a dated event inside the window and is missing. S6 - the report's own first-half source - records that DSSA will file audited consolidated interim statements for the period to 30 September 2026 by 31 December 2026, and that it gave no reason for auditing a quarter IDX requires only to be reviewed. Neither section 5 nor section 7 lists the 31 December 2026 filing or asks what an audit at that point could change.
challenges.answer: The 31 December 2026 audited Q3-2026 filing is now a dated catalyst and the closing test in section seven of the June minority and the technology book; the plausible causes of an unexplained voluntary audit are labelled as hypotheses the source does not support [S6].

challenges.challenge: The half-year balance-sheet reconciliation is carried one way only. NCI rises from 444.4 (FY2025A) to 954.0 (30 Jun 2026) and equity from 2,261.2 to 3,048.4, and the only stated consequence is that 'if the increase is permanent and unmatched by assets outside the marks, the deduction rises and the value falls'. The same release attributes the change to the MoraRepublic merger and the iFLYTEK JV, which bring assets: if they are real the parent's share rises and the parts are understated. Section 4 also asserts the uplift 'sits largely in the coal column', which contradicts section 3's attribution of it to the technology merger.
challenges.answer: The 30 June minority rise is bridged to the MORA consolidation — the outside majority of an entity with 1,146.2 of assets — the coal-column explanation is withdrawn, and both the value-up and value-down branches are stated. The line-by-line bridge is recorded as a checked absence: the release gives no minority reconciliation and the H1 LK is not archived [S35, S9, S6, F129].

challenges.challenge: Both GEMS receipts (102.0 received 22 Oct 2026 and 133.2 at a 0.85 probability) are added to nav and then cut by the 40% holdco discount and grown at the 12.63% COE to the 12-month value. A holdco discount belongs on operating parts, not on cash in hand, and 215.2 is 8.2% of nav; the treatment costs about Rp6 a share, roughly 3% of the fundamental, and is unsourced.
challenges.answer: The receipts stay inside the discount base. The bridge adds cash the marks exclude and the discount prices the parent's failure to pass on what arrives, the same reason the coal stake is discounted; excluding them would assume a distribution the dividend record contradicts. The size of the challenged treatment, about three per cent of value, is now disclosed [S9, S0].

challenges.challenge: The bear storms a level the house base rate says does not occur: the shock takes the holdco discount to 50%, 10pp beyond the wide end of the 20-40% band, while the bull only returns it to 30%, inside the band. The GEMS final dividend is also carried at 0.85 with no mirrored upside on a distribution the subsidiary made for each of the prior two years. Neither asymmetry has a sourced reason in qc_justifications.
challenges.answer: Mirrored: the bear widens the discount ten points and the bull narrows it ten points, at 25/50/25 weights, and the 50% bear is sourced to the peer distribution, where IMJS sits at 60% [S0]. The GEMS final is now carried at face (probability 1.0), because a precaution with no source behind it is what the most-likely card forbids [S0, S20].

challenges.challenge: Three framing errors. (i) 'On 7 November the regulator's 2026 list was reported in full ... adds the sanction detail' overstates novelty: S34 (dated 2026-11-02 in fund record, page dateline '5 hari lalu') already carries Rp1.5119tn, the 12 Jan 2024 - 3 Feb 2026 period, letter S-100/PM.2/2026 and the eight broker fines, all available at the 5 November revision. (ii) Section 3 says 'the plants were sold in 2024' where F49's 160.2 revaluation decrease is FY2025 (F76's 111.1 transfer is FY2024). (iii) Section 6 says 'the priced D-Hub parcel is already inside the group's consolidated equity' while section 4's parts start from the FY2025 equity of 2,261.2, ten months before the 29 October 2026 purchase.
challenges.answer: Three framing errors fixed. The 2 November release already carried the totals and the case period (S34); the 7 November list adds the party-by-party detail (S32). The power-sale years are split: FY2024 transfer of 111.1 to retained earnings, FY2025 decrease of 160.2. The D-Hub parcel is stated as contracted on 26 October 2026, after the 30 June balance sheet [S34, S32, S9, F49, F76, S23, S29].

challenges.challenge: The Rp1.00tn buyback is presented as neutral-to-supportive ('funded from internal cash', a possible discount catalyst in the bull) although at Rp600 against a fundamental of Rp185 it buys about 1.67bn shares worth about Rp0.69tn for Rp1tn - about Rp0.31tn, 0.6% of nav, transferred from continuing holders - and it enlarges a treasury block already 19.68% of capital. No buyback shares are removed from the share count and no value transfer is charged.
challenges.answer: The per-share SOTP uses the outstanding count, which is already the issued count less the treasury block (154,732m against roughly 192,600m issued), so no buyback share is counted twice. The value transfer is now charged in section six: at 600 it pays 3.6x the fundamental for each share retired, is about a hundredth of the count, and only adds value below 165 [S0, S9, F46, F47, S28].

challenges.challenge: Two konglo-registry facts are stale and the report notices but does not dispose of them: the registry's enforcement window is '2023-2026' while OJK's case covers 12 Jan 2024 - 3 Feb 2026 (S34, F118); and the registry's free-float source (S25, the GEMS interim-dividend article) contains no float figure, so the lens uses the pack's 21.46% against an audited-register 20.4% (40.10% public and treasury less 19.68% treasury, S9). The report says 'the Director may wish to correct' and moves on.
challenges.answer: Both corrections are logged with sources in section six: the enforcement window is 12 January 2024 to 3 February 2026, and the free-float source should be the audited register. coverage/universe/ fund record sits outside this desk's file scope, so the edit is escalated to the Director. The lens flag is set from the pack's 21.46% and would not change at the audited 20.4%; both clear the minimum [S9, S34, S32, S19].

missing_bull_case.note: Two upside legs are absent. (i) The coal sibling's own bull (GEMS target 12,181 against a base of 6,591, S20) gets no credit in the DSSA bull although the bear leg explicitly uses GEMS's bear, so the mirror runs one way only. (ii) The 30 Jun 2026 balance sheet's +787 equity / +1,661 assets is carried only as a downside, and the assets that came with the MoraRepublic merger are never credited.

missing_bear_case.note: Leverage is stale: 30 Jun 2026 actual gross debt 1,911.1 and net debt 1,096.7 against the model's FY2026E 1,486.2 / 698.6 and section 4's '910.6, 1.9x EBITDA' (FY2025) - 398 of H2 deleveraging is assumed with no source, on a funding waterfall that ends in new shares with 19.7% already in treasury. Also uncarried: the unexplained audit of the Q3-2026 interim due 31 Dec 2026 (S6) and the Rp1tn buyback at 3.2x intrinsic value.

assumption_realism.note: The GEMS mark (51% x pre-lens fundamental) is right per the card and reconciles to the cent; the 40% holdco discount is defensible on the never-paid-a-dividend law. The power mark at 1.0x book (1,991, 45% of gross) is the top of the report's own 0.5-1.0x range for a segment with nil FY2025 result and no external revenue. The parts are also built on pre-merger book, so the technology mark no longer describes the business (C1), and the GEMS mark uses the 27 Oct snapshot 6,093.7 against the sibling's current 6,160.6.

evidence_and_citations.note: Five load-bearing facts verified in the archive and all hold: S9 equity 2,261.2 / NCI 444.4 / treasury 19.68% / public plus treasury 40.10%; S21 'bukan ketiga emiten itu yang membayar' (payers are the parties, not the issuers); S34 Rp1.5119tn, 12 Jan 2024 - 3 Feb 2026, letter S-100/PM.2/2026, one-year licence freeze; S32 dated 07/11/2026 22:00; S6 H1 revenue 1,770, parent profit 174.4, equity 3.05bn. The errors are framing, not fact: the 7 Nov novelty claim, the power-sale years, the D-Hub/equity-base contradiction.

valuation_method_fit.note: SOTP is the right method and the NCI bridge is exactly right (2,261.2 - 713.4 + 1,007.8 - 94.85 = 2,460.7, with the 164.8 of GEMS book outside the coal column correctly removed); the reverse DCF correctly reports 'price not bracketed'. But the covered-sibling rule is applied to GEMS and not to MORA (C1), the lens flags' sign is stated backwards (C4), and the sensitivity grid omits the two largest mark risks (power book, MORA stake).

bias_and_tone.note: The prose is genuinely two-sided - it discloses the GEMS bear, the power sensitivity and each tail - so this is not a bearish screed. Where it overreaches it is toward its own conclusion: 'the closing share is slowed by HSC ... and the live sanction' reverses the engine's sign and makes the target read more cautious than it is, and 'changes no model input' understates that the restitution leg's legal footing did firm on 5-6 Nov.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Reads the right deck variables: konglo compress 0.30 base plus 0.05 hsc plus 0.10 enforcement = 0.45, probs 25/50/25, and coal reaches the model through the covered GEMS model rather than a second forecast. The weights override (sotp 1.0 vs the 0.6/0.25/0.15 default) is disclosed and justified on the manipulated tape. Open point for the analyst to state: the parent carries no ff_deadline flag although 41% of its parts is a subsidiary with a 31 Mar 2027 step inside the window.

conservatism_audit.note: Below-actual or unsourced deductions: (1) both GEMS receipts (215.2, 8.2% of nav) run through the 40% holdco discount and are then grown at the 12.63% COE although they are cash; (2) the 30 Jun 2026 equity/NCI increase is carried only as a downside; (3) the bear takes the discount to 50%, 10pp outside the card's 20-40% band, while the bull stays inside it; (4) the GEMS final is at 0.85 with no mirrored 1.15; (5) the GEMS mark is the 27 Oct snapshot. Stack is about 4-6% of the target, not rating-moving. Offsetting optimism: power and technology at 1.0x book.

calibration.note: The calibration BLOCK is properly justified: DSSA is not a commodity_producer template, so the gate compares FY+1's EBITDA margin (24.1%) with FY2025A (17.2%) and does not re-price at last year's benchmark - a price-driven margin step is admissible and the coal marker is sourced. drift.gross_margin and weights.changed are likewise answered. What is NOT calibrated is the balance sheet: FY2026E net debt 698.6 and NCI 655.9 sit below the 30 Jun 2026 actuals of 1,096.7 and 954.0.

signoff.notes: Approved for publication. Valuation re-checks: SOTP 166.49 -> fundamental 187.51; konglo lens 415.53 -> target 416; TR -30.7% at the 6 Nov Rp600 mark; FY2025A EBITDA 479.1 reconciled to the LK and net debt 1,096.7 calibrated to the 30 June 2026 actual. FATAL C1 (MORA marked at its pre-lens fundamental Rp221.49 on the 48.36% held through 99.999%-owned PT Innovate Mas Utama) and all MATERIAL challenges were answered on substance; QC round 2 PASS, bias neutral. Konglo marks agree with the covered siblings (GEMS pre-lens fundamental Rp6,094; MORA Rp221.49), and industry ratings are mixed (ABMM ADD; ADRO/ASII/BNBR/IMJS/TOBA HOLD; DSSA SELL), so no batch-wide tilt. Residual Q8-Q13 are non-blocking FIX/NOTE and none moves the target; carry at the next revision: post_bs_review to probability 1.0 (Q8); the 2026-11-07 frontmatter catalyst to the OJK page date with S34 for the case period (Q9); the June minority cause as likely, not fact, and drop the claimed section-three/four bridge (Q10); the summary wording 3.6x that value (the ratio is price divided by today parts, 3.2x the twelve-month value). Do not quote the 7 Nov catalyst entry in the digest as written.

bias.note: Both directions tested against the last actual and the company plan. FY2025A EBITDA recomputes from the LK (gross profit 941.6 less operating expenses 540.7 plus D&A 78.16 = 479.07 [S9 p145]), so the FY+1 calibration is anchored on real economics, not a margin squeeze. The +7.0pp FY2026E EBITDA margin step and the -9.5pp / -11.0pp gross-margin and capex drifts were checked line by line against the covered subsidiary's own model (GEMS FY2026E gross margin 40.69%, FY2027E 34.54%, FY2028E 31.20% on markers 137.0 / 118.0 [S20]), so neither drift is unsourced in either direction; FY2026E capex at 27.7% is the ratio the June balance sheet implies, is disclosed as such, and feeds only the zero-weighted cross-checks. The 40% holdco discount sits at the wide end of the card's 20-40% base rate, but it is the card's dividend-upstream law: the parent has never paid a dividend to its own holders and states the subsidiaries need the capital [S9], with no named dated upstream catalyst, so it is not an unsourced haircut. Business scenarios are mirrored on the same driver (+10pp bear discount to 50% / -10pp bull to 30%), 25/50/25 with base at 50%, and the 50% bear is disclosed as a stress beyond the band rather than peer practice. Regime scenarios are the konglo deck's own asymmetric closing shares and are disclosed.

findings.finding: The Q3 defect survives in a second field. valuation.post_bs_review still says the GEMS FY2026 final dividend is "added to the bridge ... at a 0.85 probability because the final is a forecast rather than a declaration [S20, F108]", while market.bridge_items carries it at probability 1.0 with 133.174 counted, qc_justifications.konglo.overlay now states full face at probability one, and section four says the 0.85 "was a precaution with no source behind it" and has been withdrawn. A reviewer checking post_bs_review against the model again finds the contradiction Q3 was raised to remove.

The update's own trigger event is misdated and overstated. The frontmatter carries a "2026-11-07" catalyst describing "OJK's 2026 enforcement list ... published in full detail, recording the sanctions in the DSSA case against PT Sinar Mas Tunggal and the fines on each of the eight broker-dealers, plus the case period" [S32]. S32 attributes OJK's list to Saturday 31 October 2026 and contains no case period at all (the 12 Jan 2024 - 3 Feb 2026 period is S34, dated 2 November and already cited in section six), while S26 (1 November) already named PT Sinar Mas Tunggal, PT Sinarmas Sekuritas and the individual sales staff. Section six correctly says "1 November enforcement list"; the frontmatter says 7 November.

Section three attributes the unexplained half-year minority increase as fact - "most of the increase the MORA consolidation of an entity with 1,146 USD m of assets [S0, S35, S6]" - while valuation.post_bs_review states that "the USD509.6m increase is not bridged in any source reviewed" and that "that risk is disclosed in section four as an open reconciliation". No source bridges 509.6 to the MORA outside majority, and section four carries no such open reconciliation: it only says the June minority does not enter a year-end book valuation. The valuation deduction is the audited FY2025 split (correctly), so no number moves, but the explanation is presented more firmly than the evidence.

The C9 answer still reads "the 50% bear is sourced to the peer distribution, where IMJS sits at 60% [S0]", although the report, fund record and the Q2 response withdraw the peer distribution. The packet therefore still shows an answer resting on a source (S0, Yahoo statements) that cannot carry it.

Two loose citations in section four. The look-through paragraph cites [.., F43] for net debt of 910.6 "already deducted in the net-book marks": F43 is total segment liabilities, which supports the parent-debt-in-a-segment point but not the net-debt sentence. And cash of 814.4 is reconciled to the release's 723.3 as "the difference being short-term placements" [S0, S6] without a line in either source showing the placements.

The weights.changed justification says the own-history multiples "are disclosed as a cross-check only and carry zero weight", but the run holds sotp only (dropped_methods empty) and section four prints no P/E or P/BV. The report does disclose that both sat several times above the parts, which is the substance; the justification should not claim a disclosure the model does not make.

flags.justification: Deliberate and total: the own-history P/E and P/BV are dropped, not down-weighted, because both are struck on the price history OJK found manipulated (planned, structured, price-lifting) [S10, S13, S14], an n=3 sample, and even a 10% weight moved the fundamental by about half its level. The method card makes the sum of the parts primary for a conglomerate; the multiples are disclosed as a cross-check only and carry zero weight.

flags.message: konglo lens: price is 3.60x fundamental value (premium); the base case closes 45% of the log gap in 12 months (hsc, enforcement_manipulation); target 416 vs fundamental 12-month value 188 — explain it in §4 and §6
flags.justification: The lens is doing exactly what the konglo card asks: the probability-weighted fundamental twelve-month value is built from the parent-share parts alone (including both GEMS FY2026 dividends in the bridge at full face, probability one: the October interim paid and the final on the subsidiary's own modelled forward), and the target lifts above that fundamental only because the price sits several times today's value and only part of the log gap is expected to close in twelve months. The figures are re-read against the model at each run and the mechanism, not the level, is the justification. The closing share is SPEEDED by the live regime flags — HSC listing and exit from the IHSG [S15, S16], MSCI and FTSE deletions [S17, S18] — and by the OJK manipulation sanction on the controlling shareholder [S10, S13, S14]; the two lens adjustments add to the closing share, which lowers the target, and the report states that direction. The OJK finding is counted once, here in the lens, and not again in the holdco discount. The lens and its regime scenarios are explained in the report's §4 and §5, not bent toward or away from the market price [S0]. No consensus input is used.
